title: Rural Home Loans: Limit on Country Home Loans Held by One Member
content:
**Clause.** A member may hold at most 2 Country Home loans at a time in applied, active, forbearance or nonaccrual status, and at most one for each occupancy under the occupancy aggregation rule of the Rural Home Loans program; an investment or rental property is not financed as a Country Home loan at all.

## The clause restated

| Element | What the clause fixes |
|---|---|
| Who | One member, across all of that member's Rural Home Loans |
| What is counted | Country Home loans in applied, active, forbearance or nonaccrual status |
| Most held at a time | 2 |
| Per occupancy | at most one, under the occupancy aggregation rule |
| Property never financed | an investment or rental property |

## Points of judgement

- A loan in applied status already counts toward the 2; the count is not limited to funded loans.
- *Hypothetical case:* a member holds one active Country Home loan on a primary residence and has one application in applied status for a second home. The member holds 2 loans in the counted statuses, which is the most the clause allows.
- *Hypothetical case:* a member asks to finance a house bought to rent out. Under the clause a rental property is not financed as a Country Home loan at all, whatever the member's other holdings.
